page: Microsoft Azure L8s_v2 is an LSv2-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7551 processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and includes 2002 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the L8s_v2 exhibits lower-tier compute and memory bandwidth capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 10% of benchmarked servers. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, both read and write, also falls into the bottom 10%, though small-block cached read bandwidth performs slightly better, placing in the bottom 25%. Passmark CPU and memory scores register in the middle 50%, showing average performance for general integer and encryption workloads, while database operations and Redis SET operations fall into the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L8s_v2 offers a high local storage-to-vCPU ratio and a dense memory profile without the premium cost of high-tier compute processors. The trade-off lies in its modest CPU execution speeds and constrained memory bandwidth. This configuration is suitable for storage-heavy workloads, database hosting, and basic data processing tasks that require significant local storage capacity and moderate memory but do not demand high-frequency CPU performance.
